title: Lindsey Graham addresses energy policy and support for Trump in March 2026 posts - Greenville Leader
text:
Senator Lindsey Graham, representing South Carolina in the U.S. Senate, posted a series of statements on March 23, 2026, addressing energy policy and national leadership. The tweets emphasized his support for former President Donald Trump and highlighted themes of energy independence and strong governance.
In one post made at 15:14 UTC, Graham wrote: “Democrats want you to accept weaker energy, weaker leadership and policies that defy common sense. President @realDonaldTrump needs a fighter in his corner, and he knows he can count on me.”
Later that day at 16:41 UTC, Graham continued to discuss energy policy with another statement: “Excellent reminder, Mr. President, of the benefits of energy independence that have been achieved on your watch. An energy independent America is a safer America. 47 and his team are doing a great job.”
At 17:31 UTC on the same day, Graham posted: “Hey Tehran Tom, you might want to call Baghdad Bob and see how all that worked out.”
Lindsey Graham has served as a colonel in the U.S. Air Force Reserves for 33 years and has chaired the Senate Budget Committee (official website). He also serves on key Senate Committees including Appropriations, Judiciary, and Environment and Public Works (official website). A native of Central, South Carolina who grew up in a blue-collar family operating a local restaurant and pool hall (official website), Graham holds undergraduate and law degrees from the University of South Carolina (official website). His legislative focus has included fiscal responsibility and national security.
